prompt:
Create one abstract logo for KITE. Exact text (copy verbatim, no other words): ''. Exact slogan: ''.
Render only the supplied exact text and nonempty slogan; the brand context is not additional lettering. Empty strings request no corresponding text.
Industry: independent travel planning. Audience: curious explorers.
Styles: abstract folded geometry. Original brief palette context: Vermilion #DD513D, Background: solid pure white #FFFFFF.
Avoid: unsolicited lettering, mockup scenes, watermarks, colored canvas, transparent background, external cast shadows. Use cases: Brand identity at 240px width and README previews.
Background: opaque. Produce a real PNG raster image. Use clean, readable shapes at small sizes; leave safe margins. Do not draw a transparency checkerboard, mockup, watermarks, or a concept grid.
Concept direction: Independent travel with a sense of taking a new route: one abstract folded shape made from two broad vermilion planes, forming a lifted asymmetric diamond silhouette with one clean diagonal white passage. Rounded optical adjustment at the single very sharp point; all other edges clean and deliberate. The shape suggests flight without a literal kite, airplane, arrow, trail or string. Flat one-color compact symbol, no text, no shading and no enclosing tile.. Assumptions: Fictional demonstration brand; new concept approved for one sample by the user., All new showcase images must have a genuine opaque white background., Foreground palette is design intent, not exact-pixel certification..
Logo construction: Build a nonliteral abstract mark around the concept's geometric or organic gesture, with coherent weight, deliberate openings and a memorable silhouette. Use style references for broad construction traits, not their brand words or traced signature shapes. The identity should remain recognizable in a one-color silhouette at the intended use size. This construction check does not replace the requested palette or request an extra monochrome image.
Lettering fidelity: preserve every Unicode character, capitalization, punctuation, space and reading order in the applicable text. Keep Hangul syllable blocks intact; do not translate, romanize, abbreviate or substitute lookalike glyphs. Shape changes must keep required text readable, including counters and joins at the intended size.
